participants.name: Curry Citizen
participants.professional_persona: Curry Citizen, a retired furniture manufacturing supervisor with three decades of carpentry and lean‑process expertise, now channels their practical curiosity into mentoring apprentices, volunteering as a safety trainer, and running a modest handyman side business while flexibly adapting schedules to community projects.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Curry has three decades of experience in the furniture manufacturing sector of High Point, where he progressed from a skilled carpenter to a production supervisor. He combines hands‑on woodworking with lean process improvement, budgeting, and rigorous safety compliance. His leadership style blends clear organization with the flexibility to adjust production schedules on the fly. Beyond the factory floor, Curry is adept at conflict mediation, community event coordination, and basic home electrical and plumbing repairs. He stays digitally literate, comfortably using email, online banking, and senior‑friendly social media platforms to stay connected and learn about new DIY technologies.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: Now retired from full‑time work, Curry aims to channel his expertise into mentorship and community service. He plans to volunteer as a safety trainer for local vocational programs, mentor apprentices in woodworking, and launch a modest handyman side business to supplement his pension. He also hopes to document his career journey and the history of Black workers in the regional furniture industry in a memoir. Maintaining his health, managing stress, and supporting his wife and grandchildren are central to his long‑term ambitions.

participants.name: Sarah Chen
participants.professional_persona: Sarah is a nonparticipating anesthesiologist who works on a freelance basis at multiple surgical centers in California. She relies on the Act to avoid surprise billing penalties while negotiating fair rates for her services.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Skilled in regional anesthesia and perioperative pain management, with a strong understanding of QPA calculations and IDR processes.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: Sarah seeks to build a network of ambulatory surgery center contracts that provide stable income, reducing her reliance on out-of-network claims.

participants.name: Maria Gonzalez
participants.role_anchor_entity_id: GroupHealthPlanOrIssuer:Group Health Plan or Health Insurance Issuer
participants.professional_persona: Maria is a health plan manager for a mid-sized group health plan in Texas, overseeing the implementation of out-of-network payment standards. She coordinates with provider networks to ensure timely payments and accurate cost-sharing for enrollees.

participants.name: Dr. Alisha M. Torres
participants.role_anchor_entity_id: RegulatoryAgency:Federal Regulatory Departments (HHS, DOL, Treasury, OPM
participants.professional_persona: Alisha is a senior policy advisor at the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) with over a decade of experience in health insurance regulation. She leads the team drafting the interim final rules for the No Surprises Act, ensuring they align with statutory authority while addressing stakeholder concerns.
participants.skills_and_expertise: Expert in federal rulemaking processes, cost-sharing methodologies, and quantitative analysis of out-of-network payment data. She also has deep knowledge of the Qualified Payment Amount (QPA) calculation and its impact on provider networks.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: Alisha aims to become the director of the CMS Center for Consumer Information and Insurance Oversight, where she can shape broader consumer protections in healthcare. She is also passionate about mentoring junior analysts from underrepresented backgrounds.

participants.name: David Kim
participants.role_anchor_entity_id: IndependentDisputeResolutionEntity:Independent Dispute Resolution Entity under No Surprises Act
participants.professional_persona: David is a former emergency department physician who now works as an independent dispute resolution entity, bringing firsthand clinical insight to payment disputes. He understands the medical necessity arguments that underpin many out-of-network claims and can quickly assess the reasonableness of charges. His medical background lends credibility with both providers and plans.
participants.skills_and_expertise: He has a unique combination of clinical knowledge and business acumen, having also run a small medical practice. He is skilled in reviewing medical records and billing codes to evaluate appropriate reimbursement levels.
participants.career_goals_and_ambitions: David wants to bridge the gap between clinical care and health plan administration by promoting evidence-based payment models. He plans to speak at medical conferences about the impact of surprise billing on patient care.
